profile.themes: KFC Turnaround via Value Strategy; Merger Arbitrage with Devyani; LPG Cost Inflation; Sri Lanka Macro Recovery

deepdive.sec: Indian QSR Franchisee & Multi-Brand Food Services

bull_bear.body: Priority on organic store expansion and refurbishments; Merger-related costs (INR6.6cr) incurred for employee retention/ESOP modification; No dividend commentary; Focus on deleveraging via EBITDA growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: LPG availability and pricing volatility (25-40% cost increase); Raw material inflation; Pizza Hut India structural underperformance; Merger execution risk (NCLT/SEBI/CCI approvals pending 7-10 months); Sri Lanka macro/geopolitical instability.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident on KFC strategy validation ('finally got it right'); Cautiously optimistic on consumer demand despite peer caution; Transparent on one-offs; Pragmatic on inflation pass-through; Long-term focused on merger synergies.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Vendor partners are cross-subsidizing the INR99 value meal (fries/beverage suppliers) to gain volume, masking true gross margin impact which could emerge later; The 'renewal fee' component of capex is a hidden structural cost increase as the franchise matures past 10 years; KFC's own delivery app is outperforming aggregators significantly, reducing commission drag over time.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Optimal capital allocation is stated to drive the new restaurant expansion model, with a focus on smaller sized omni-channel restaurants.
- Average restaurant size has been cut by ~45% for both brands — KFC from 2,736 sq ft as of 31-Mar-19 to ~1,500 sq ft currently, and Pizza Hut from 2,427 sq ft as of 31-Mar-19 to ~1,200 sq ft currently.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: KFC India: Revenue +15%, SSSG +4% (+6% ex-Navratri), Rest EBITDA margin 16.8% (+110bps QoQ); Pizza Hut India: Revenue -6%, SSSG -7%, Rest EBITDA margin -3.3%; Sri Lanka: Revenue +15% LKR, SSSG +11%, Rest EBITDA margin 14.6% (pressed by minimum wage hikes).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as YUM's franchisee operator in India, Sri Lanka and Maldives, and as Sri Lanka's largest international QSR chain (footnoted as in terms of Restaurant Sales for FY21 and number of restaurants operated as of March 31, 2021).
- The Sapphire Story frames two global brands (KFC and Pizza Hut) with scale and profitability among the Top 3 QSR operators, an execution mindset combining customer experience with back-end operational excellence, and 'capability and capital to drive growth'.
- Value-based work culture, high on governance, enabled by professional management, board and promoters.
- Geographic reach: KFC and Pizza Hut operate in states covering 56% of GDP (footnoted as FY19 GDP contribution of states where restaurants are located), are present in 10 and 11 Indian states respectively and in 5 and 6 of India's Top 8 cities respectively; the Top 8 cities contribute 87% of the Chain Food Services Market (FY20).
- Deck states 488 restaurants of both KFC and Pizza Hut are operated across 34 cities.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Merger] Note on the deck states that on 1st Jan 2026 the boards of directors of Sapphire Foods and Devyani International approved a merger scheme, subject to statutory and regulatory approvals from various authorities.
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June 2026: Promoters & Promoter Group 39.2%, Foreign Portfolio Investors / Non-Resident Indians 26.1%, Domestic Mutual Funds and Insurance Companies 25.3%, AIF, Resident Individuals & Others 9.4%.
- [Assurance] Internal audit by Protiviti, statutory audit by Deloitte, and ESG assisted by PWC (the deck's only ESG reference).
- [Governance] Board chaired by Sunil Chandiramani (Independent Director), with Sanjay Purohit as Whole Time Director and Group CEO and Vijay Jain as Executive Director and CFO; brand leadership split between a CEO - KFC and a COO - Pizza Hut.
- [Disclosure] Deck links to the Sapphire Foods Annual Report 2025-26 as the fuller reference document.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin supported by vendor partnerships on value meals; Risk of 50-70bps GM pressure if vendor support withdraws; LPG inflation impacting EBITDA by 30-50bps; Marketing spend increased by 75-100bps to drive recruitment; Minimum wage hikes in Sri Lanka offset operating leverage.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: FY27 Capex expected to match FY26 levels (~INR320cr); KFC SSSG trajectory targeting mid-single digits sustained by new strategy; No immediate price hikes planned unless raw material/oil costs spike dramatically; Merger completion expected by end of FY27 (12-15 month process from Jan 2026 announcement).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A - Retail restaurant model; Store expansion pipeline includes 73 KFC openings in FY26 (total 575) and 9 Sri Lanka openings; FY27 capex guided similar to FY26 driven by new stores, refurbishments, and renewal fees.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Merger with Devyani International to create unified largest QSR player in India; Sri Lanka expansion accelerating (9 stores in FY26, highest in 3 years) with potential for high single/low double digit additions next 2-3 years; Digital kiosk rollout (73% complete) driving APC uplift.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Sapphire Foods delivered its strongest quarter in 3 years with KFC SSSG hitting 6% (ex-calendar) driven by a permanent INR99 value layer and behavior-changing advertising, validating the turnaround strategy just as the complex merger with Devyani International enters the final regulatory approval phase. While Pizza Hut India remains challenged, the Sri Lanka business continues to defy macro volatility with double-digit growth, positioning the combined entity for dominant market share post-merger.
